RG-c3bf21b6df.description: Division may fail when the divisor is zero
RG-c3bf21b6df.rationale: The divisor is a variable and this expression does not establish a non-zero precondition.

LLM-0f164820ab.description: Uses a mutable default argument causing shared state across calls
LLM-0f164820ab.rationale: The default dict is created once at function definition time, so successive calls share and accumulate entries unintentionally

LLM-c576c07cfa.description: Uses eval on arbitrary input, enabling code injection
LLM-c576c07cfa.rationale: An attacker can supply malicious Python code that will be executed with the program's privileges

LLM-cd05c7b133.description: Executes user‑provided command with shell=True, allowing command injection
LLM-cd05c7b133.rationale: Shell interprets special characters, so an attacker can inject additional commands or alter execution flow
LLM-cd05c7b133.suggested_fix:
def run_user_command(argument):
    return subprocess.run(argument, shell=False, check=True)

RG-e403dcb056.description: Function uses a mutable default argument
RG-e403dcb056.rationale: The same mutable object is reused across calls, which can leak state between invocations.

LLM-5df683b1c9.description: Division by zero possible when count is zero
LLM-5df683b1c9.rationale: Calling average with count=0 raises ZeroDivisionError, causing the program to crash

LLM-851dc5af3e.description: Uses eval on arbitrary input, enabling code execution
LLM-851dc5af3e.rationale: eval will execute any Python code supplied in the expression, creating a severe security vulnerability

RG-baa36383e0.description: Use of eval can execute attacker-controlled Python
RG-baa36383e0.rationale: Dynamic code execution is unsafe when any part of the expression is untrusted.
RG-baa36383e0.suggested_fix:
return ast.literal_eval(expression)
# import ast; literal_eval accepts only Python literals. For arithmetic, parse with ast and allow only number and operator nodes.

RG-7663bfe20f.rationale: Shell command parsing can enable command injection if arguments contain untrusted data.
RG-7663bfe20f.suggested_fix:
return subprocess.run(shlex.split(argument), shell=False, check=True)
# import shlex; better still, accept a list and allowlist the program name.

LLM-b99269807f.description: Division by zero if count is zero
LLM-b99269807f.rationale: An attacker can supply count=0 causing a ZeroDivisionError, leading to denial of service.

LLM-b44ab68306.description: Mutable default argument creates shared state across calls
LLM-b44ab68306.rationale: The default dict is created once at function definition time, causing unexpected persistence and potential memory bloat.
